query: Explain why some Qatar Airways Business-Class flights receive a non-recommended (Recommended = no) result.

per_column.name: crew_service_inconsistency
per_column.rationale: Encodes whether/how cabin-crew service failed (poor attentiveness, rude, disorganized, inconsistent). This is a candidate cause whose effect on non-recommendation is being attributed, i.e. a treatment. Not a common cause of another treatment and the outcome, so not a confounder.

per_column.name: price_value_perception
per_column.rationale: Encodes value/price judgments (price high for decline, unjustified for product, premium for old aircraft). Another candidate driver of the recommendation decision, i.e. a treatment. It is a perception on the way to the outcome, not a background common cause adjusted to de-bias another treatment.

per_column.name: traveler_type_expectation_mismatch
per_column.rationale: Although the label evokes a pre-treatment trait (traveler type), all realized values are dissatisfaction/friction/mismatch expressions (operational friction, coordination issue, separation complaint) that lie on the path from experience to non-recommendation. Adjusting for this would block part of the causal effect, so it functions as a mediator, not a confounder.

judge.rationale: The operator supplies several candidate causes of non-recommendation (crew service failures, price/value perception) and one mediating dissatisfaction channel, but it does NOT supply any genuine confounder — a variable that jointly causes one of the treatments AND the outcome and must be adjusted to remove attribution bias (e.g., aircraft age/configuration, route or load, fare class/price paid, seasonality). The added columns form a parallel multi-cause / mediator decomposition rather than a confounder-controlled causal-estimation design. Because the decisive test asks whether real common causes were surfaced from the data/text, and none were, the causal-attribution claim is not satisfied.
